source.title: Does LLM Pre-Training Typically Occur at the Edge of Stability?
source.authors: Yu-Hang Cai; Hao-Dong Wen; Hao-Feng Huang; De-Yi Liu; Yi-Yuan Ma; Kaifeng Lyu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses local quadratic simulations and curvature measurements to test when edge-of-stability behavior occurs during stochastic and adaptive training. It does not measure training classification error or the loss-recovery dynamics in V5.
record.gate_note: Results about local quadratic stability and EoC/EoS bear on training dynamics, but they do not measure whether the trained models recover from an above-threshold learning rate and reach low training loss. Figure-only diagnostics are not transcribed as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures curvature and finite-horizon stability of compensated quadratic surrogates during minibatch SGD and AdamW training. These results do not directly test any stated version. In particular, V5 includes full-batch edge-of-stability behavior as well as loss recovery, but the study does not measure its specified full-batch sharpness-and-loss trajectory or recovery relative to the initial linearized stability limit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate when interpreted across tested runs rather than every checkpoint. The authors find EoC consistently across LLM pretraining configurations and EoS frequently but not universally. Small batches and sufficiently reduced learning rates can remove EoS; excessive peak rates can place training above the estimated quadratic threshold. These conclusions concern their generalized local-surrogate diagnostics.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes local quadratic surrogates around checkpoints from GPT-style language-model pretraining with AdamW, rather than testing the stated classification-error or learning-rate-recovery recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: EoS varies with batch size, learning-rate schedule and peak learning rate; EoC weakens at small learning rates during decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Compensated quadratic simulations frequently transition from bounded displacement to explosion near the training learning rate. This transition depends on batch size, learning-rate schedule and model scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic neural-network training often operates near an estimated stability threshold of compensated local quadratic dynamics, with substantial dependence on training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Negative effective curvature can make uncompensated local quadratic dynamics unstable at every positive learning rate while actual neural-network training remains stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persistent negative curvature creates a learning-rate-independent failure of local quadratic approximations during neural-network training.

fits_no_version.finding: At peak learning rate 0.04, the estimated quadratic critical learning rate averages approximately one tenth of the training rate; final evaluation loss is higher, and Figure 13 separately reports actual GPT-large training-loss trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Actual AdamW language-model training can continue above a compensated quadratic surrogate's estimated stability threshold, with worse loss at excessively large learning rates.

record.problems: The central EoS detector uses finite-horizon, single-trajectory local simulations and a compensation estimate; the authors state that this differs from the expected detector analyzed theoretically. Their bounds require assumptions, including that the compensated mean is positive definite, which the estimated compensation alone does not verify. The experiments concern local quadratic surrogates rather than recovery of actual training loss after an LR overshoot.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were retained because the reported outcomes concern local quadratic stability or curvature, not the training-error or actual-loss-recovery behavior named by V1–V6. Quantitative plots without a corresponding textual outcome were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of activation-matched, orthogonal or Gaussian initialization on training speed and trainable depth.

Recovery after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks; full-batch sharpness approaching and hovering at the stability threshold while loss falls; actual training divergence despite starting below that threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Retaining no claim-linked rows is appropriate. The reader's V5 rationale was incomplete because V5 also includes full-batch edge-of-stability behavior. Nevertheless, the stochastic surrogate measurements do not directly test that clause. The detector's guarantees concern an expected diagnostic with different initial conditions from the implemented single-trajectory diagnostic (Appendix A.3). Absence of stochastic EoS therefore does not challenge the explicitly full-batch claim.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, and stopping or regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual networks, depth effects, and training error.
Initialization choices, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

The version's specified recovery sequence—loss rise after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit followed by low training loss—is not measured. The paper studies divergence thresholds of local quadratic surrogates, not recovery of the actual training loss after an LR overshoot.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
